name: Mosaic
desc: A hand-set tessellated floor running away to the vanishing point, laid in true andamento — the courses of tesserae flow in rings around a central emblema and bend as they pass it rather than gridding the floor, every little stone is cut askew and sits on its own bed so it takes the raking light on its own facet, and lacunae have opened where the floor failed and been patched flat with modern screed; Roman bone-and-ochre, a Byzantine gold ground that flashes, austere monochrome, a dusty fresh excavation, or a cyan setting-out plan.

energy.doc: how hard the raking light works the floor — facet flare on every tessera, the flash off gold, and the scroll rate

scale.doc: tessera size in world units — at min a vermiculatum fine enough to draw a face, at max coarse pebble work

density.doc: how much dust drifts low over the floor in the light

speed.doc: how fast the floor streams toward the viewer and the next panel arrives

ruin.doc: how far gone it is — grout width, and how much of the floor has fallen away into screed-patched lacunae

hue.doc: hue of the stone the tesserae are cut from

x.doc: vanishing point x as a canvas fraction

y.doc: horizon y as a canvas fraction — everything above it stays fully transparent so the bg shows through

style.doc: aesthetic: Roman domestic work in bone, ochre, terracotta and basalt / a Byzantine gold ground with jewel glass, the gold set askew on purpose so it flashes as the light crosses / austere monochrome, the drawing carried by value alone / a fresh excavation, everything still under a film of dust and only half revealed / a cyan setting-out plan — the andamento as pure line, no stone at all

seed.doc: workshop lottery — which stone each tessera is cut from, how askew it is set, where the floor has failed
